name: workflow_is_living_design
content: Workflow design is continuous learning, not one-time specification. It operates at three interconnected levels: static_design (explicit documented procedures), dynamic_design (real-time adaptation during execution), and learning_design (feedback mechanisms that enable improvement). The workflow is a living_pattern maintained through feedback_loop cycles where practitioners observe, identify patterns, experiment, and capture learning. Adaptation_patterns range from micro-adjustments within a service to structural redesigns over years. The three design levels form a reinforcing cycle: learning_design enables dynamic_design, which generates feedback that refines static_design, which feeds back into learning_design. Improvement emerges from feedback_loop operating across multiple time_scales, progressing through improvement_trajectory stages. Without learning_design, workflows stagnate; without dynamic_design, they become brittle; without static_design, learning dissipates.
